newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Polish c.banker not unhappy about last zloty slide.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.banker not unhappy about last zloty slide.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz on Monday said she was not unhappy about the zloty's weakening since the last days of May, sparked by the Czech crown's steep drop.

Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the weaker zloty, which lost one percent against the basket of currencies as a result of the crisis in Czech financial markets, would help keep Poland's rapidly widening current account gap in check.
"In light of the current account, when the zloty depreciated, we were not unhappy," Gronkiewicz-Waltz told Reuters in an interview at the Bank of International Settlements annual meeting in Basle.
Gronkiewicz-Waltz declined to predict possible future movements of the zloty, but said downward pressure on the zloty coming from withdrawing currency speculators has ended.
"There was a certain pressure, but it is finished now," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.
The zloty now stands at about 1.5 percent above the central parity rate, down from about 2.5 percent in mid-May. @

Foreign investor withdrawal from the Czech Republic and Central Europe in general pushed the zloty to an all-time low against the basket at even with the parity rate before the Polish currency rebounded.

Gronkiewicz-Waltz said Poland's foreign exchange mechanism, which ties the zloty to a basket of five Western currencies and a steady devaluation factor, was satisfactory and said that no plans to modify the regime were in the works.
